report_meta: Shows how well primers match relevant target sequences. Use the report to identify primers that may need review. The documentation tab explains the calculations and how to interpret the values.
primer_overview_note: First review primers marked Watch, High or Critical (Review level criteria is given in documentation tab). Click a primer name to open its details. Check which sequences have no hit or several mismatches, and whether mismatches occur near either primer end.
risk_criteria_note: The review level is an automatic screening signal. It does not by itself mean that the assay has failed. Confirm important findings with assay performance data and laboratory context.
primer_investigation_note: For each primer, first check the summary values and the mismatch-position chart. Then review the mismatch distribution and the individual sequences.
risk_watch_title: At least one no-hit result is present, or a hit has two or more mismatches.
risk_high_title: One or more high-level review thresholds are met.
risk_critical_title: One or more critical-level review thresholds are met.
terminal_share: Hits with mismatch in the selected terminal region
ngs_note: Each amplicon is checked for at least one LEFT (forward) and one RIGHT (reverse) primer with a Low or Watch level. Alternative primers provide backup. If either side has no such primer, the amplicon is marked Critical in this overview.
no_viable_primer: no primer at Low or Watch level
chart_title: Mismatch position and observed sequence base
chart_empty: No mismatch-position data are available for the current selection.
chart_note_what: Each bar is one position in the primer. Bar height is the percentage of hit comparisons with a mismatch at that position. Each color shows the base observed in the sequence.
distribution_note: The chart groups comparisons by 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4+ mismatches. No-hit comparisons are shown separately. Percentages use all filtered comparisons for this primer.
no_data_mismatch_count: No mismatch-count data are available for the current selection.
sample_rows_sorted: Showing {visible} of {total} comparisons. No-hit comparisons are shown first, followed by hits with the most mismatches. Select a sequence ID to open the primer-sequence alignment when available.
lower_priority_hidden: {count} additional comparisons are hidden. Show all to inspect them.
no_rows_match: No comparisons match the current filters.
no_alignment: No accepted alignment is available for this comparison. Check the input sequence and the matching criteria before interpreting this as a primer problem.
col_Terminal_Mismatch_Share: Hits with mismatch in selected terminal region
doc_intro: Use this report to see how well each primer matches the uploaded sequences. It is a screening tool: it helps you decide what to inspect, but it does not decide whether an assay has failed.
doc_use_1: Choose an organism or virus, primer or FASTA file if you want to limit the report. Leave the filters at All to review the complete data set.
doc_use_2: Start in the Primer overview. Review primers marked Watch, High or Critical before primers marked Low.
doc_use_3: Click the primer name. Check the no-hit rate, highest mismatch count and the proportion of hits with 2+ or 3+ mismatches.
doc_use_4: Use the mismatch-position chart to see whether the same positions are affected in many sequences, especially near the primer ends.
doc_use_5: Check individual no-hit sequences and sequences with several mismatches. Open the alignment when it is available.
doc_use_6: Before changing a primer or assay, assess the finding together with sequence quality, assay validation, Ct trends, controls, epidemiology and other laboratory information.
doc_faq_1_q: Which results should I check first?
doc_faq_1: Start with primers marked Watch, High or Critical. Open their details and check which sequences, mismatch counts and primer positions caused the level.
doc_faq_2: One comparison is one primer checked against one relevant sequence from the FASTA input. A sequence may therefore appear once for each primer that was tested against it.
doc_faq_3: No hit means that no alignment between the primer and sequence passed the current matching criteria. Possible reasons include true sequence differences, a partial or low-quality sequence, missing sequence at the binding site or unsuitable input. It is not by itself proof of assay failure.
doc_faq_4_q: What do identity and mismatch count mean?
doc_faq_4: For a hit, mismatch count is recalculated using a full-primer alignment. Local BLAST hits are extended with adjacent sequence bases where available; incompatible bases and missing bases represented by gaps count as mismatches. Reported identity is 100 × (primer length − mismatch count) / primer length.
doc_faq_5_q: What does mismatch in the selected terminal region mean?
doc_faq_5: It is the percentage of hit comparisons with at least one mismatch in the selected terminal region. For primers, this is the last five bases at the 3' end; for probes, it is the first five bases at the 5' end.
doc_faq_6_q: Does High or Critical mean that the assay has failed?
doc_faq_6: No. These levels are automatic review signals. Interpret them together with assay validation, Ct trends, control results, epidemiology and laboratory context.
doc_faq_7_q: Why can the review level change when I use a filter?
doc_faq_7: The level is recalculated from the comparisons left after filtering. A primer can therefore have a different level in a selected subset than in the full data set.
doc_term_hit: Hit: an accepted alignment was found between the primer and the sequence.
doc_term_no_hit: No hit: no alignment passed the current matching criteria.
doc_term_mismatch: Mismatch: a base in the observed sequence does not match the compatible base or IUPAC code in the primer.
doc_term_identity: Identity: for hit comparisons, 100 × (primer length − recalculated mismatch count) / primer length. This is recalculated by Primer Checker, not the raw BLAST percentage identity.
doc_term_terminal: Terminal mismatch rule: for primers, only the last five bases at the 3' end are counted; for probes, only the first five bases at the 5' end are counted.
doc_filters_text: Filters update all visible cards, tables and charts. The review level is recalculated after the organism/virus, primer and FASTA filters are applied.
doc_cards_1: Comparisons: the number of primer-sequence comparisons left after filtering.
doc_cards_2: Primers: the number of unique primer names in the filtered data.
doc_cards_3: Sequences: the number of unique FASTA sequence IDs in the filtered data.
doc_cards_4: Hits and No hits: the numbers of accepted and unaccepted alignments.
doc_cards_5: Mean identity (%): the mean identity of hit comparisons only. No-hit comparisons are excluded because they have no accepted alignment.
doc_overview_text: The table summarizes the current filtered data for each primer. Select a column heading to sort the table.
doc_overview_1: Review level: the highest automatic level reached by the primer under the current filters.
doc_overview_2: Comparisons, Hits and No hits: the total number of comparisons and their match status.
doc_overview_3: No-hit rate: no-hit comparisons divided by all comparisons for the primer.
doc_overview_4: Highest mismatch count: the largest full-primer mismatch count among hit comparisons.
doc_overview_5: Mean identity (%): the mean percentage identity among hit comparisons.
doc_overview_6: Hits with 2+ or 3+ mismatches: the percentage of hit comparisons with at least two or at least three mismatches.
doc_overview_7: Terminal-region mismatch share: the percentage of hit comparisons with at least one mismatch in the role-specific terminal region: the primer 3' end or probe 5' end.
doc_risk_text: The level is calculated separately for each primer from the filtered comparisons. If several rules apply, the highest level is shown. The thresholds prioritize review; they are not validated assay-failure limits.
doc_risk_critical: Critical: no-hit rate is at least 20%, hits with 3+ mismatches are at least 25%, or hits with a role-specific terminal mismatch are at least 50%.
doc_risk_high: High: no-hit rate is at least 5%, hits with 2+ mismatches are at least 30%, or hits with a role-specific terminal mismatch are at least 5%.
doc_risk_watch: Watch: at least one no-hit comparison is present, or the highest mismatch count is at least 2.
doc_risk_low: Low: none of the Watch, High or Critical rules are met.
doc_panels_text: Each primer panel combines the summary values, hit rate, mismatch-position chart, mismatch-count distribution and sequence table. Use these parts together: a percentage is easier to interpret when you also know the number of comparisons behind it.
doc_chart_text: Each bar represents one primer or probe position. Its height is the percentage of hit comparisons with a mismatch at that position. Colors show the base found in the sequence. The y-axis is adjusted to the data in each chart, so check the axis before comparing charts. Red marks show the role-specific terminal region: the last five bases at the 3' end for primers, or the first five bases at the 5' end for probes.
doc_distribution_text: This chart groups comparisons into 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4+ mismatches. No-hit comparisons have a separate category. Counts and percentages use all filtered comparisons for that primer.
doc_detail_text: The table shows the FASTA file, organism or virus, sequence ID, segment, match status, identity, mismatch count, mismatch positions and base changes. No-hit comparisons are shown first by default. Select a sequence ID to open the primer-sequence alignment when alignment strings are available.
doc_alignment_text: The primer is shown above the observed sequence. A vertical line marks a compatible base. Empty positions indicate a difference. The Base differences line lists the recorded mismatch positions and base changes.
doc_workflow_1: Each selected primer is aligned with every relevant FASTA sequence using BLASTn.
doc_workflow_2: For each primer-sequence pair, the alignment with the fewest recalculated mismatches is kept; the higher BLAST bit score breaks a tie. If BLAST returns no usable alignment, the comparison is marked no_hit internally and shown as No hit.
doc_workflow_3: A local BLAST hit is extended to the full primer length using adjacent sequence bases, reverse-complemented where needed. Mismatches are then recalculated, including incompatible bases and unavailable bases represented by gaps. Omitted ends are not automatically mismatches when compatible adjacent bases can be recovered.
doc_workflow_4: Compatible IUPAC ambiguity codes are treated as matches. For example, primer base Y is compatible with C or T in the sequence.
doc_workflow_5: Mismatch positions start at 1 at the primer’s 5′ end. Base changes are shown as position:primer base>sequence base, for example 9:T>A.
doc_ngs_text: This section appears only for NGS panels with recognized LEFT and RIGHT primer names. Alternative primers are treated as backup. A side is available when it has at least one primer at Low or Watch level. If no such LEFT or RIGHT primer remains, the amplicon is marked Critical in this overview. This is a screening rule, not a direct measurement of amplicon performance.
doc_limits_1: The report only assesses the sequences included in the current input. It may not represent all circulating variants or all samples tested in the laboratory.
doc_limits_2: A partial, low-quality or incorrectly labelled sequence can produce mismatches or a no-hit result.
doc_limits_3: The review rules simplify primer performance. They do not model every effect of mismatch position, chemistry, primer concentration, probe performance or assay conditions.
doc_limits_4: A Low level does not guarantee assay performance, and a High or Critical level does not prove assay failure.
doc_limits_5: Confirm important findings with appropriate laboratory data and, when needed, manual sequence review or experimental testing.
terminal_share_primer: Hits with mismatch at primer 3' end (last 5 bases)
terminal_share_probe: Hits with mismatch at probe 5' end (first 5 bases)
chart_note_use_primer: Look for repeated mismatches and high bars. Red marks identify the last 5 bases at the 3' end of primers. Only mismatches in this region contribute to the terminal-mismatch metric.
chart_note_use_probe: Look for repeated mismatches and high bars. Red marks identify the first 5 bases at the 5' end of probes. Only mismatches in this region contribute to the terminal-mismatch metric.
